tagline.text: Pagsanjan's diocesan shrine of Our Lady of Guadalupe, founded in 1687

children.text: Pagsanjan Church is the main parish church of Pagsanjan, Laguna, founded in 1687 by a Franciscan missionary. It is said to be the oldest church in the Philippines under the patronage of Our Lady of Guadalupe, and was declared a diocesan shrine in 2012.

The church's formal name is Our Lady of Guadalupe Parish Church. It stands in the Poblacion (town center) of Pagsanjan, Laguna, and is a Diocesan Shrine in the Diocese of San Pablo. English Wikipedia describes it as the oldest Philippine church under the patronage of Our Lady of Guadalupe. The town even calls itself the "Home of Our Lady of Guadalupe de Filipinas."

Its history goes back to November 12, 1687. The Franciscan missionary Fr. Agustin de la Magdalena came as the first parish priest and founded the parish; until then Pagsanjan had been a small chapel district (visita) of neighboring Lumban. The first church, built in 1688, was a light structure of bamboo, nipa palm and wood, raised by forced labor of the townspeople. In 1690 it was replaced by a larger adobe church with a red-tiled roof. In the 19th century, from 1847 to 1852 under Fr. Joaquin de Coria, a stone belfry and a Romanesque dome were added, and in 1872 a transept was built. On March 15, 1945, during World War II, bombing heavily damaged the church and destroyed the original image of Our Lady of Guadalupe. A replica was then built over the ruins and fully restored in 1965, and on April 6, 1969 Bishop Pedro Bantigue blessed the church and consecrated the main altar. The church you see today was rebuilt without its old dome.

This is less a flashy tourist attraction than a living church where parishioners still attend Mass. It fits well before or after a Pagsanjan Falls boat trip or a Laguna church pilgrimage (Visita Iglesia), and entry is free. The highlights are the three-level facade, the three-story bell tower, and the Mexican relics in the small Guadalupe Tilma Chapel beside the altar. Please keep quiet during Mass.
Wikipedia gives December 12, 1668 as the founding date of the town of Pagsanjan, which took Our Lady of Guadalupe as its patron. It lies about
100km

from Manila, which makes it a good day trip. Pagsanjan is best known for its falls and boat rides, but adding the church helps you understand the town's faith and Spanish-era story. The church's story is tied to the town's formation. A small settlement that was a visita of Lumban became an independent parish in 1687, and records say the image donated by the first priest was enthroned on the altar the following year on December 12. The Mexican relics in the Tilma Chapel and the image donated by Mexican Catholics in 1958 show that this long connection continues today.

The facade is in the Early Renaissance style on three levels, with a semicircular arched entrance, a choir loft window and a triangular pediment. On the left stands a three-story square bell tower topped with a dome, easy to spot from Pagsanjan's town center. For photos, the plaza in front lets you fit the whole tower into one shot.

blocks.title: A church rebuilt after the war

children.text: After bombing heavily damaged it in 1945, a replica church was built over the ruins and restored in 1965. Pagsanjan natives living in Manila are said to have helped with fundraising and rebuilding, and today the church stands rebuilt without its old dome.

blocks.title: Images of Our Lady of Guadalupe

children.text: The original image, donated by the founding priest and enthroned on the main altar on December 12, 1688, was destroyed in the 1945 bombing. In 1958 Mexican Catholics donated a life-size image carved by Ramon Barretto of Toluca, and the main altar holds an image carved after the war by Maximo Vicente of Manila.

A small side chapel beside the altar holds an image of St. Juan Diego, a replica of the tilma (cloak) on which Our Lady appeared, and a stone relic from Tepeyac Hill in Mexico City. It also serves as a small museum of liturgical vestments worn by Pagsanjan priests. The Tilma Chapel feels smaller and older than the main church, a quiet place to linger.

blocks.title: Diocesan shrine declaration and works since 2013

children.text: In 2012 the Diocese of San Pablo declared the church a diocesan shrine. From 2013 the patio (forecourt), choir loft and church gate were built. A Catholic directory site also lists it among the Jubilee churches for the 500 Years of Christianity in the Philippines and the Holy Years (2016 and 2025).

A historical marker from the Philippine historical commission is said to have been installed in 1953. It tells of the church's long history, so look for it near the entrance. Check on site for its current condition.

blocks.title: December 12 feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe

children.text: The parish feast is the solemnity of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12. Around this date, Masses and processions make the area around the church busiest, and you can see parishioners' devotions up close. Event schedules change every year, so confirm with the parish.
The patio and gate renovated since 2013 make a good spot for photographing the exterior. It is also a place to rest for a moment away from the noise of the town center.

items.title: Day trip from Manila
items.subtitle: The church together with Pagsanjan Falls

children.text: Leave Manila and take a bus toward Santa Cruz, Laguna. The trip to Pagsanjan takes
about 2 hours
or so and can take longer depending on traffic.
Arrive at Pagsanjan town center and head to the church by tricycle or jeepney.
Look over the facade, bell tower and forecourt, then go inside to see the main altar and the side altars.
In the Guadalupe Tilma Chapel beside the altar, see the image of Juan Diego, the tilma replica and the display of liturgical vestments.
Have lunch at a restaurant in the town center.
Take the
Pagsanjan Falls
boat trip. The falls trip takes nearly half a day, so it is better to see the church in the morning.

During Mass, avoid walking around inside and look around after Mass ends. On days when you combine the church with the falls, finish the church in the morning. As a diocesan shrine, it draws more visitors on Sundays and feast days.
Start at Pagsanjan Church. Walk slowly around the church grounds and the chapel.
Travel to other nearby Laguna churches by rental car or chartered vehicle. Decide which churches to visit on site to suit your schedule.
Have lunch and rest.
Visit nearby heritage towns such as
Pila Heritage Town
From Manila to Pagsanjan is about
100km
, taking
around 2 hours
depending on road conditions.
Buses run from Manila toward Santa Cruz, Laguna, and from Santa Cruz to Pagsanjan it is about
6km
by tricycle or jeepney.
Fares, timetables and departure terminals change often. Check at the local boarding area before you leave.
A 2016 travel blog advised taking a Santa Cruz-bound bus from Taft Avenue and getting off at Pagsanjan. Routes may have changed since, so check the latest information.
Travel via SLEX and Laguna provincial roads toward Santa Cruz. Enter "Pagsanjan Church" or "Our Lady of Guadalupe Parish Church" in your navigation app.
The street in front of the church can be narrow and crowded, so check on site whether parking is available.
In Pagsanjan's town center people get around by tricycle and jeepney. The church is in the town center, a short ride from the falls landing area.
It is safer to confirm the fare before boarding.

The church can be visited all year, but the November–May dry season is more comfortable. Around the December 12 feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe it is liveliest with Masses and events, and also most crowded. You can visit at any time of day, but we recommend going in the morning or late afternoon to avoid midday heat.
Showers are frequent in the rainy season (June–November). The church and chapel visit is little affected, but Pagsanjan Falls trips may change with higher water, so check ahead.

Pagsanjan is usually a day trip from Manila, but if you want to combine the falls trip with nearby towns, you can stay in Pagsanjan's town center or in Santa Cruz. Check prices and reviews on a booking platform. Seeing the church alone takes about an hour, but with the falls and a stroll through town, allow half a day to a full day. Leave early in the morning so you do not miss the falls trip by arriving late.

Meals are easy in the town center's restaurants and snack shops. You can easily find places selling local snacks in front of the church and in the center; sticking to long-established places is a safe choice. Restaurants around the church get busy at lunchtime, especially right after Mass. Many places prefer cash, so carry small bills.
This is still an active parish church. Please avoid loud noise and flash photography during Mass.
Mass times differ by source and are not reliable. Check parish announcements and the notice board in front of the church.
Clothes covering shoulders and knees are recommended rather than shorts or sleeveless tops.
The chapel inside the church may be closed at some times.
If you are also doing the Pagsanjan Falls trip the same day, see the church first in the morning.
Traffic is heavy on the December 12 feast and during major Catholic events, so leave early.
When taking photos, be considerate and avoid capturing worshippers' faces during Mass.
Locally the church is also called "Pagsanjan Church." This name is easy to use when asking for directions.
The parish phone number differs by source; if you need to call, use the parish's official contact information.
Mass schedules and transport fares differ by source and change often. Check the latest information with the parish and locally before you go.
Follow local instructions on photography inside the church.
Watch your belongings in the crowded town center.
The chapel and museum area may not have fixed opening hours.
Bring an umbrella in months with frequent showers.
Avoid transport that overcharges tourists, and confirm the fare before boarding.
Dates differ slightly by source, such as the 1687 founding and the 1688 first building, so read the on-site markers and the parish's explanation together.
Laguna's signature falls trip, reached by boat from the town center, and easy to combine with the church on the same day.
